transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE); Maya Singh (Redwood CSM); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Sofia Chen (BlueNexus, VP Eng); Liam O'Neill (BlueNexus, Platform Ops); Priya Raman (BlueNexus, ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Quarterly health check focused on service economics, upcoming capacity for Q4, reliability guardrails and compliance artifacts. Action: benchmarking run + cost breakdown + security docs.

[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this tight, about 45-60 minutes, planned agenda is usage, incidents, capacity planning for next quarter, and then guardrails & security.
[00:12] Sofia Chen: Awesome. Yep, we've got time. Liam, Priya are on in case we need deep infra questions.
[00:18] Liam O'Neill: hey, hi. Good to see you all. Quick note — last week's incident where inference latency spiked, we want to understand root cause + mitigation.
[00:26] Diego Alvarez: yeah, I pulled traces; looks like a combo of a KV cache miss storm and autoscaler thrash when the batchers tried to spin up. There was also a small NFS throttling event on their side but that contributed.
[00:40] Priya Raman: I think the cache pattern changed after a new feature push — more long-format prompts, so sequence length distribution shifted which spiked tokens and changed batching behavior.
[00:56] Maya Singh: to clarify, when you say KV cash miss — you mean the prefix cache, right? sometimes the transcription says K-V cash, sorry these notes are messy.
[01:06] Diego Alvarez: yes, prefix/KV cache. Our runtime expects certain reuse; when prompts widen the reuse falls off and you get more per-token compute.
[01:18] Jordan Park: okay, before we get deep — quick numbers Sofia promised: overall token usage + peak RPS for last 30 days?
[01:26] Sofia Chen: sure, we're seeing a 38% month-over-month increase in embedding calls, text gen steady at +12% and peak RPS about 2.6k last Tuesday during daylight hours. Costs are up roughly 21% compared to forecast.
[01:40] Jordan Park: thanks — that matches what we see in console. Important for cost talk: are those embeddings on dedicated endpoints or hosted?
[01:48] Priya Raman: embeddings are on hosted for now, text gen is mix of hosted and dedicated pools. We have two dedicated slices for conversational model.
[01:56] Liam O'Neill: question — with Q4 coming (holiday surge), what's the runway for our current reserved capacity? Will we exhaust burst?
[02:04] Diego Alvarez: based on current throughput, you'll be at 78% reserved utilization during median hours, spikes could hit 110% peak without burst. We recommend bumping reserved capacity or enabling short-term burst credits — depending on if you want cost predictability or cheaper pay-as-you-go.
[02:20] Sofia Chen: can you quantify tradeoffs? like cost delta if we move 20% of embeddings to dedicated vs keep hosted?
[02:28] Maya Singh: yes, we'll run a cost-by-route breakdown. Preliminary: embeddings at scale usually save on per-token when pinned to quantized dedicated instances but you lose flexibility; hosted is simpler but marginally more expensive at sustained volumes.
[02:46] Priya Raman: also need to consider model variants — we might switch to a smaller embedding model for long-tail queries, which reduces tokens and cost but may impact downstream matching quality.
[02:58] Jordan Park: let's capture that in the bench. Diego, can Redwood run a 72-hour bench that replays our peak-day traffic including the longer prompts?
[03:06] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can. We'll need the peak-day traffic CSV and a flag on sequence-length distribution. If possible, provide real payloads or sanitized versions. The bench will measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, GPU utilization, and how autoscaler behaves under burst.
[03:22] Sofia Chen: we can sanitize and share by Monday. Priya, can you pull the sample?
[03:26] Priya Raman: yep, I'll get that done.
[03:28] Liam O'Neill: about SLA guardrails — can Redwood enforce fallbacks to smaller model family automatically when latency targets breach? We want graceful degradation rather than errors.
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: absolutely, we have routing policies: latency-first or cost-first. We can set a policy that fails over to a quantized variant or smaller model and also cache prefix aggressively for those fallbacks. There's also region-based fallback if a zone is congested.
[03:52] Sofia Chen: we need to document exact SLOs and what counts as a breach. Our compliance folks want auditable rollbacks.
[03:58] Jordan Park: agreed — we'll produce a guardrail playbook that lists thresholds (p95 > X ms for Y minutes triggers fallback), observability hooks, and alerting.
[04:10] Maya Singh: reminder to include cost guardrails too: e.g., if daily token spend > budget threshold, throttle lower-priority routes. Would you want auto-throttle or just alerts?
[04:22] Liam O'Neill: auto-throttle with human override for ops critical flows.
[04:26] Priya Raman: note: we have a regulatory set of customers that must stay within EU-only regions; any routing that moves them to other regions is not allowed.
[04:34] Diego Alvarez: that's fine — we can pin region and also enforce model variants only within allowed regions. For private deployments, we can bring the full control plane on VPC.
[04:44] Jordan Park: security ask — Sofia mentioned SOC2 and VPC architecture diagram. We'll send both. Anything else on compliance?
[04:52] Sofia Chen: encryption-at-rest details and KMS integration; also audit log retention periods — we need 1 year of immutable logs for certain tenants.
[04:58] Maya Singh: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and we can configure log forwarding to your SIEM. Retention policies can be adjusted, but immutable retention might require a compliance add-on. We'll include options.
[05:12] Priya Raman: one more technical: quantization profiles — we've been testing 4-bit across some models and seeing occasional hallucination spikes — any suggestion?
[05:22] Diego Alvarez: quantization helps cost but can affect output distribution. Suggest per-workload evals; Redwood Optimize recommends profiles by workload and has automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to prompt sets. We'll include recommended configs for your top 10 prompts.
[05:36] Jordan Park: competitor check — you mentioned AICoreCloud earlier, any reason they'd be attractive?
[05:42] Sofia Chen: their pricing is cheaper for burst but they don't offer the same VPC-private package and their observability is weaker. There's also GigaServe; they do on-prem but support is limited.
[05:52] Maya Singh: noted.
[05:54] Liam O'Neill: on capacity — what's the lead time to provision new dedicated slices? If we decide to add 30% reserved, how long?
[06:02] Diego Alvarez: typically 3-5 business days for capacity in our hosted pools; for dedicated reserved contracts, depends on contract & infra procurement — can be same week if capacity available, or 2-3 weeks otherwise.
[06:16] Sofia Chen: okay, that's tight but manageable. We might want a temporary burst credit while dedicated procurement completes.
[06:24] Jordan Park: we'll propose a multi-step plan: 1) run 72-hour bench; 2) cost-by-route + guardrail configs; 3) SOC2 + VPC diagram; 4) execute short burst credit and reserve increase if bench shows need.
[06:38] Priya Raman: sounds good. Also, can we get token-level breakdowns by route for last 90 days? That will help forecast.
[06:46] Maya Singh: yes, I'll export token-level by route and share as CSV.
[06:50] Sofia Chen: perfect. Any other blockers?
[06:54] Liam O'Neill: one ask: can Redwood provide a runbook for our NOC that describes steps during a latency incident — how to flip routing, who to call, rollback steps?
[07:02] Diego Alvarez: yes, Diego will author an incident playbook and share as markdown.
[07:08] Jordan Park: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners.
